meta.title: Persona Intake Form
meta.subtitle: Captures everything needed for the hub's AI to authentically represent this person — voice, judgment, decision style, ownership-facing approach.
meta.save_strategy: auto-save per field on blur; localStorage fallback; explicit Submit promotes to data.personas[slug]

sections.title: A. Identity & Role
sections.description: Who you are, who you report to, and the scope of what you own.

fields.label: Full name
Preferred name / what you go by
fields.placeholder: e.g. Tim, not Timothy

fields.label: Current title
Department
Reports to (name + title)
fields.placeholder: e.g. Samir Lakhany — President

fields.label: Direct reports — names + roles + count
fields.placeholder: List who reports to you, by name. If 10+ indirect, summarize.

fields.label: Years in current role
Years with Superhost
Years in hospitality
Geographic / regional scope you cover
fields.placeholder: States, regions, or specific properties you own day-to-day

fields.label: Brand families you have direct expertise in
Certifications, designations, specializations (e.g. CHA, MBA, CPA)

sections.title: B. Domain & Authority
sections.description: What you own. What you don't. The decisions that need someone above you.

fields.label: Primary domains you own (pick all that apply)
Decisions you can make unilaterally (no escalation needed)
fields.placeholder: Be specific: dollar thresholds, decision types, vendor approvals, hiring level...

fields.label: Decisions that need Samir / Ash / Board sign-off
Things you DON'T own / always defer to a peer (and to whom)
fields.placeholder: e.g. Legal disputes -> Kori; capital allocation -> Samir

fields.label: Key vendor / partner relationships YOU personally manage
fields.placeholder: e.g. Hilton FQM contacts, M3 account exec, primary insurance broker

sections.title: C. How You Read Data
sections.description: When a report lands on your desk, what do your eyes go to first? What triggers you to act vs monitor?

fields.label: First metric you check on any report
fields.placeholder: e.g. NOI flow-through vs plan

fields.label: Second metric you check
Third metric you check
Variance thresholds — what makes you monitor vs call the GM vs treat as crisis?
fields.placeholder: e.g. 'RevPAR -5% I monitor, -8% I call the GM, -12% it's an emergency'. Repeat for the metrics that matter to you.

fields.label: How do you sequence analysis?
options: GM-first (talk to the GM, then look at numbers)

fields.label: Rank the comparisons that matter most to you (1 = most important)
Things in a report that make you roll your eyes
fields.placeholder: e.g. 'Hiding bad news in the third paragraph', 'Citing variances without dollar magnitude'

fields.label: Common analytical mistakes you see others make

sections.title: D. How You Respond to Ownership
sections.description: The mechanics and the style of your owner-facing communication. Get this right and the persona reads like you.

fields.label: Default reporting cadence with owners you cover
Format preference for owner updates
Detail level you default to
How do you deliver bad news in writing?
options: Soften with a positive framing first
Pick up the phone instead of writing

fields.label: How do you handle owner pushback on a recommendation?
Things you NEVER put in writing to owners
Your go-to opening line for an owner update
fields.placeholder: e.g. 'Three things to know about [property] this period:...'

fields.label: Calibration notes for specific owners — anything the persona must know about how to talk to a particular ownership group
fields.placeholder: e.g. 'Lakhany prefers oral updates; Capitol One wants written; Gulfstream cares more about balance sheet than P&L...'

sections.title: E. Voice & Style
sections.description: How you sound in writing. The single most important section for the AI to land your voice.

fields.label: Sentence length you default to
Formality (1 = casual / 10 = lender-grade formal)
Industry / brand jargon
options: Plain English always — define any acronym
Insider language when it's more efficient
Insider always — assume the reader knows the lingo

fields.label: Phrases or expressions you use often (give us 5-10)
fields.placeholder: e.g. 'The call is...', 'What we know vs what we believe', 'Let me be direct...'

fields.label: Phrases or words you'd NEVER use
fields.placeholder: e.g. 'synergy', 'leverage' (as a verb), 'circle back', 'deep-dive', 'bandwidth'

fields.label: Use of humor
Emotional register
Three words you'd use to describe how you sound
fields.placeholder: e.g. Direct, dry, owner-fluent

fields.label: How do you typically open and close a written deliverable?
fields.placeholder: e.g. open with 'The headline:'; close with 'My ask:'

sections.title: F. Decision-Making Style
sections.description: How you decide. Speed, risk, what info you need, how you communicate disagreement.

fields.label: Risk tolerance (1 = conservative / 10 = aggressive)
Decision speed
options: Fast trigger — decide on first read

fields.label: What information do you need before you can decide?
fields.placeholder: List the 3-4 items. e.g. 'Dollar magnitude, precedent, who owns execution, downside if I'm wrong'

fields.label: How do you communicate disagreement — with peers, with reports, with ownership?
Tell us about a recent decision you made (anonymize if needed) — what data, what process, what outcome
fields.placeholder: 200-400 words. The persona will use this as a model for how you reason.

sections.title: G. Strategic Priorities
sections.description: What's actually on your mind right now. Refresh this section quarterly.

fields.label: Top priority this quarter
Second priority
Third priority
Top operational frustration right now
Second frustration
Third frustration
Three things you'd change about the portfolio if you had a free hand
Properties getting extra attention from you right now — name them and why
Owners you have particular insight on — what does the persona need to know about each?

sections.title: H. Voice Training Samples
sections.description: The persona learns your voice by example. Spend the most time here. Write naturally — paste actual past examples if you have them.

fields.label: Walk-through: how would you diagnose a sudden 10% RevPAR drop at one property over a single week?
fields.placeholder: Write 5-8 sentences in your own voice. The persona uses this as the canonical 'how this person reasons aloud' sample.

fields.label: Sample owner email: an owner asks 'why did GOP miss plan?' — draft your reply in your own voice
fields.placeholder: 100-200 words. Real or hypothetical, doesn't matter — what does matter is that it sounds like YOU.

fields.label: Sample team conversation: a GM tells you turnover spiked 6 points last month — your response on a call
fields.placeholder: Capture the real spoken cadence — short turns, follow-up questions, how you push.

fields.label: Sample memo opener: write the first 2-3 sentences of a strategic memo you'd send up to Samir/Ash on a topic you've been chewing on
Sample board comment: write the talking points you'd say out loud presenting your function's update to the leadership team (1-2 minute version)
Optional — link to any past public writing in your voice (LinkedIn post, press quote, internal memo we can pull)
fields.placeholder: Pasting a URL helps the persona calibrate further.

sections.title: I. Constraints & Boundaries
sections.description: What the AI persona MUST NOT say or do in your name. Treat as the legal-and-ethics fence.

fields.label: Topics the persona should NEVER opine on (defer to a real person)
fields.placeholder: e.g. capital structure, refinancing, personnel terminations, ongoing litigation, individual guest complaints

fields.label: Topics that ALWAYS require escalation to a real person — and to whom
fields.placeholder: e.g. brand-letter formal response -> Kori; owner termination notice -> Samir; lender covenant question -> CFO

fields.label: Confidentiality boundaries — what the persona must not write down in any output
Standard disclaimers you always include on certain types of output (e.g., on draft owner memos, on capital recommendations)
Specific scenarios where the persona must explicitly say 'this needs the actual [name]' rather than answer
fields.placeholder: e.g. anything involving an active EEOC charge; any dollar number going on a signed PIP response

sections.title: J. Personal Touches (optional but recommended)
sections.description: Small things that make the persona feel like a real person, not a job description. Keep it human.

fields.label: An industry mentor or hero who shaped how you think
Best book on hospitality or leadership you'd hand a new GM
A word you know you overuse
A question you wish more people asked you
Best time of day to do real thinking
Preferred channel for non-urgent things
Anything else the persona should know about you that wasn't asked
